stories-5-32-killing-one-soul-is-as-if-k.title: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 After Cain and Abel: Saving or Killing One Soul
stories-5-32-killing-one-soul-is-as-if-k.note: Surah 5:32 moves directly from Cain killing Abel in 5:27–31 to a decree for the Sons of Israel that killing one person is like killing all mankind and saving one is like saving all mankind, matching the rabbinic homily on Genesis 4:10 in Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God revealed this legal principle to the Children of Israel in their ancient scriptures following the first human murder.
discussion.reply: In the Hebrew Bible, Genesis 4:10 records the narrative of Cain and Abel without any decree equating one life to all mankind. That maxim originates in Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 (c. AD 200), where rabbinic sages explicitly derive it as human courtroom commentary on the plural Hebrew word for bloods (demei) in Genesis 4:10.

stories-5-32-killing-one-soul-is-as-if-k.quranEn: From that time We prescribed for the Sons of Israel that whoever kills a person, except (in retaliation) for another, or (for) fomenting corruption on the earth, (it is) as if he had killed all the people. And whoever gives (a person) life, (it is) as if he had given all the people life. Certainly Our messengers have brought them the clear signs, yet even after that many of them act wantonly on the earth.
quranHighlights: whoever kills a person, except (in retaliation) for another, or (for) fomenting corruption on the earth, (it is) as if he had killed all the people
whoever gives (a person) life, (it is) as if he had given all the people life

sources.title: Mishnah Sanhedrin
sources.en: Therefore, Adam the first man was created alone, to teach you that with regard to anyone who destroys one soul from the Jewish people, i.e., kills one Jew, the verse ascribes him blame as if he destroyed an entire world, as Adam was one person, from whom the population of an entire world came forth. And conversely, anyone who sustains one soul from the Jewish people, the verse ascribes him credit as if he sustained an entire world.
highlights: anyone who destroys one soul
the verse ascribes him blame as if he destroyed an entire world
anyone who sustains one soul
the verse ascribes him credit as if he sustained an entire world

phrases-5-45-life-for-life-eye-for-eye-t.title: Torah Citation: 'The Life for the Life, and the Eye for the Eye'
phrases-5-45-life-for-life-eye-for-eye-t.note: Surah 5:45 explicitly cites the Torah's law of retaliation ('The life for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth'), matching Exodus 21:22–25 and Leviticus 24:19–20.

discussion.view: Classical commentators such as al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr note that Surah 5:45 explicitly quotes the legal ruling God revealed to Moses in the Torah.
discussion.reply: Surah 5:45 reproduces the sequence of clauses found in the extant books of Exodus 21:23–25 and Leviticus 24:19–20 ('life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth') and calls upon the Jews of Medina to judge by the written Torah in their possession.

phrases-5-45-life-for-life-eye-for-eye-t.quranEn: We prescribed for them in it: ‘The life for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and (for) the wounds retaliation.’ But whoever remits it as a freewill offering, it will be an atonement for him. Whoever does not judge by what God has sent down, those – they are the evildoers.
quranHighlights: ‘The life for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and (for) the wounds retaliation.’

sources.title: Exodus 21:22-25 (LXX)
sources.en: But if it be perfectly formed, he shall give life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.
highlights: he shall give life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot, burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe.

sources.title: Leviticus 24:19-20
sources.en: And whoever shall inflict a blemish on his neighbor, as he has done to him, so shall it be done to himself in return; bruise for bruise, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: as any one may inflict a blemish on a man, so shall it be rendered to him.
highlights: bruise for bruise, eye for eye, tooth for tooth

practices-5-103-abolishing-pre-islamic-b.title: Abolishing Pre-Islamic Dedicated Camels: Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham
practices-5-103-abolishing-pre-islamic-b.note: Surah 5:103 abolishes four pre-Islamic Arabian classes of livestock consecrated to idols—Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham—defined in detail by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab in Sahih al-Bukhari 4623 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:103.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators cite Surah 5:103 and the Prophetic report on 'Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i to show that consecrating slit-eared or free-roaming camels to idols was a polytheistic innovation rejected by Islam.
discussion.reply: Sahih al-Bukhari 4623 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:103 preserve Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab's technical legal taxonomy of four Hijazi livestock categories—Bahirah, Sa'ibah, Wasilah, and Ham—whose milk, offspring, and backs were tabooed for local deities. The verse's four technical terms are drawn directly from pre-Islamic Arabian pastoral and sanctuary law.

practices-5-103-abolishing-pre-islamic-b.quranEn: God has not appointed any baḥ īra or sā’iba or waṣīla or ḥ āmi, but those who disbelieve forge lies against God. Most of them do not understand.
quranHighlights: God has not appointed any baḥ īra or sā’iba or waṣīla or ḥ āmi

sources.title: Sahih al-Bukhari
sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4623 (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: Definitions of Bahirah and Sa'ibah)
sources.en: Bahira is a she-camel whose milk is kept for the idols and nobody is allowed to milk it; Sa'iba was the she-camel which they used to set free for their gods and nothing was allowed to be carried on it.
highlights: Bahira is a she-camel whose milk is kept for the idols
Sa'iba was the she-camel which they used to set free for their gods

sources.title: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab on Wasilah and Ham in Sahih al-Bukhari)
sources.workSub: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab on Wasilah and Ham in Sahih al-Bukhari)
sources.en: As for the Wasilah, it is a female camel setting the first delivery as a female, then giving birth to another female at its second delivery. They used to set them free for their idols, if she connected one to the other without a male between them. As for the Ham, it is a male camel which copulates a set number of copulations, and when he finished his copulations they would leave him for the idols, exempt him from carrying burdens, so nothing would be carried on him, and they called him a Hami."
highlights: As for the Wasilah, it is a female camel
As for the Ham, it is a male camel

stories-5-31-raven-scratching-earth-to-b.title: A Raven Sent to Scratch the Earth and Show How to Bury Abel's Corpse
stories-5-31-raven-scratching-earth-to-b.note: Surah 5:31 describes God sending a raven scratching in the earth to show Cain how to bury his brother Abel's corpse, paralleling Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 22:8 where the birds of the heavens and clean beasts bury Abel's body.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators explain that because Abel was the first human to die on earth, Cain did not know how to dispose of a corpse until God sent a raven to dig in the soil before him.
discussion.reply: Genesis 4:8–10 makes no mention of birds or burial instructions after Cain slays Abel. In fifth-century Palestinian Midrash Bereishit Rabbah 22:8, Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat addresses how Abel was buried by stating that the birds of the heavens and kosher beasts buried him, a midrashic motif that precedes the next verse's citation of Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 in Surah 5:32.

stories-5-31-raven-scratching-earth-to-b.quranEn: Then God raised up a raven, scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother. He said, ‘Woe is me! Am I unable to be like this raven, and hide the shame of my brother?’ And then he became one of the regretful.
quranHighlights: God raised up a raven, scratching in the earth, to show him how to hide the shame of his brother

sources.title: Midrash Bereishit Rabbah (Genesis Rabbah)
sources.ref: Bereishit Rabbah 22:8 (Birds of the Heavens Burying Abel)
sources.en: Who buried him? Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat said: The birds of the heavens and the kosher beasts buried him, and the Holy One blessed be He rewarded them with the two blessings that one recites over them – one for slaughter and one for covering the blood.
highlights: Who buried him? Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat said: The birds of the heavens and the kosher beasts buried him

practices-5-90-91-prohibition-of-wine-ma.title: Ban on Wine (Khamr), Arrow-Gambling (Maysir), and Sacrificial Stones
practices-5-90-91-prohibition-of-wine-ma.note: Surah 5:90–91 bans wine, maysir arrow-gambling, ansab sacrificial stones, and azlam divination arrows, targeting the pre-Islamic pairing of wine and arrow-lots in 'Antarah's Mu'allaqah, the Kaaba azlam in Bukhari 1601, and ansab in Ibn Kathir.

discussion.view: Classical commentators note that God prohibited wine and gambling in stages before issuing the final categorical ban in Surah 5:90–91 alongside pagan sacrificial stones and divination arrows.
discussion.reply: Pre-Islamic poetry, including verse 54 of the Mu'allaqah of 'Antarah ibn Shaddad (~AD 580), pairs wine-purchasing with maysir arrow-casting over slaughtered camels as twin marks of Arabian chivalry, while Sahih al-Bukhari 1601 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir on 5:90 document the sacrificial stone altars (ansab) and divination arrows (azlam) used in pre-Islamic sanctuaries.

practices-5-90-91-prohibition-of-wine-ma.quranEn: [90] You who believe! Wine, games of chance, stones, and divination arrows are an abomination, part of the work of Satan. So avoid it in order that you may prosper. [91] Satan only wishes to cause enmity and hatred among you with wine and games of chance, and to keep you from the remembrance of God and from the prayer. Will you refrain?
quranHighlights: Wine, games of chance, stones, and divination arrows are an abomination

sources.title: Mu'allaqah of 'Antarah ibn Shaddad
sources.ref: Mu'allaqah of 'Antarah, v. 54 (Pre-Islamic Wine-Drinking and Maysir Arrow-Lots)
sources.en: Whose hands were brisk in casting lots, when winter demands such recreation: a man censured for his disregard of wealth, and for causing the wine-merchant to strike his flag, by purchasing all his store .
highlights: Whose hands were brisk in casting lots
causing the wine-merchant to strike his flag, by purchasing all his store

The people took out the pictures of Abraham and Ishmael holding Azlams in their hands. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "May Allah curse these people. By Allah, both Abraham and Ishmael never did the game of chance with Azlams."

sources.orig: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مَعْمَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ، حَدَّثَنَا أَيُّوبُ، حَدَّثَنَا عِكْرِمَةُ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم لَمَّا قَدِمَ أَبَى أَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْبَيْتَ وَفِيهِ الآلِهَةُ فَأَمَرَ بِهَا فَأُخْرِجَتْ فَأَخْرَجُوا صُورَةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمَا الأَزْلاَمُ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏ "‏ قَاتَلَهُمُ اللَّهُ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ قَدْ عَلِمُوا أَنَّهُمَا لَمْ يَسْتَقْسِمَا بِهَا قَطُّ ‏"‏‏.‏

sources.en: As for Al-Ansab, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ata', Sa'id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, and others said: "They were stone altars near which they would slaughter their sacrifices." As for Al-Azlam, they also said: "They were arrows that they used for lotteries to make decisions."

phrases-5-18-we-are-the-sons-of-god-and-.title: Jews and Christians Saying: 'We Are the Sons of God, and His Beloved'
phrases-5-18-we-are-the-sons-of-god-and-.note: Surah 5:18 quotes Jews and Christians saying 'We are the sons of God, and His beloved,' matching Rabbi Akiva's saying in Pirkei Avot 3:14 ('Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present') and 1 John 3:1.

discussion.view: Commentators explain that Surah 5:18 records and rejects the verbal boast of seventh-century Jewish and Christian communities claiming special filial standing before God.
discussion.reply: While Deuteronomy 14:1 and 1 John 3:1 call believers 'children of God,' the specific pairing of the two predicates ('sons of God, and His beloved') reproduces Rabbi Akiva's famous saying in Mishnah Pirkei Avot 3:14 ('Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present') and treats a metaphor of covenantal love as a literal claim to exemption from divine chastisement.

phrases-5-18-we-are-the-sons-of-god-and-.quranEn: The Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God, and His beloved.’ Say: ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins? No! You are human beings, (part) of what He created. He forgives whomever He pleases and He punishes whomever He pleases. To God (belongs) the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them. To Him is the (final) destination.’
quranHighlights: The Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God, and His beloved.’

sources.title: Pirkei Avot
sources.en: Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present. Especially beloved are they for it was made known to them that they are called children of the All-Present, as it is said: “you are children to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 14:1).
highlights: Beloved are Israel in that they were called children to the All-Present.
you are children to the Lord your God

highlights: See how great a love the Father has bestowed on us, that we would be called children of God

practices-5-6-four-part-water-ablution-w.title: Ritual Ablution (Wudu'): Washing Face, Forearms, Head, and Feet Before Prayer
practices-5-6-four-part-water-ablution-w.note: Surah 5:6 codifies the four-part pre-prayer ablution (washing face and forearms to elbows, wiping head and feet to ankles) and dry soil wiping (tayammum), paralleling Exodus 30:19–21 and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 15a.

discussion.view: Sunni and Shi'i jurists treat Surah 5:6 as the comprehensive Medinan charter for minor ritual ablution (wudu'), major ritual bathing (ghusl), and dry earth purification (tayammum) prior to canonical prayer.
discussion.reply: Washing the hands and feet with water before approaching sacred service is commanded in Exodus 30:19–21, and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 15a (~AD 500) extends this priestly washing to every layperson after relieving oneself before reciting the Shema and Amidah—adding the exact rabbinic rule that one lacking water wipes the hands with earth or a pebble.

practices-5-6-four-part-water-ablution-w.quranEn: You who believe! When you stand up for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles. If you are defiled, purify yourselves. If you are sick or on a journey, or if one of you has come from the toilet, or if you have touched women, and you do not find any water, take clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it. God does not wish to place any difficulty on you, but He wishes to purify you and to complete His blessing on you, so that you may be thankful.
quranHighlights: When you stand up for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles
if one of you has come from the toilet, or if you have touched women, and you do not find any water, take clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it

sources.title: Exodus 30:19-21
sources.ref: Exodus 30:19-21 (Washing Hands and Feet Before Approaching the Altar)
sources.en: And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet with water from it. Whenever they shall go into the tabernacle of witness, they shall wash themselves with water, so they shall not die, whenever they advance to the altar to do service and to offer the whole burnt offerings to the Lord. They shall wash their hands and feet with water, whenever they shall go into the tabernacle of witness; they shall wash themselves with water, that they die not; and it shall be for them a perpetual statute, for him and his posterity after him.
highlights: wash their hands and their feet with water
whenever they shall go into the tabernacle of witness

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot
sources.ref: Berakhot 15a (Washing Hands Before Prayer or Wiping with Earth)
sources.en: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, dons phylacteries, recites Shema, and prays, the verse ascribes credit to him as if he built an altar and offered a sacrifice upon it, as it is written: “I will wash in purity my hands, and I will encircle the altar of the Lord” (Psalms 26:6). Rava said to him: Do you not maintain, Master, that one who does so, it is as if he immersed his entire body, as it is written: “I will wash in purity,” and it is not written: “I will wash my hands”? Ravina said to Rava: My Master, look at this Torah scholar [tzurva merabbanan] who came from Eretz Yisrael and said something astonishing: One who has no water with which to wash his hands, it is sufficient that he wipes his hands with earth, a rock, or a sliver of wood.
highlights: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, dons phylacteries, recites Shema, and prays
One who has no water with which to wash his hands, it is sufficient that he wipes his hands with earth

stories-5-110-jesus-cradle-speech-clay-b.title: Surah 5 Review of Jesus' Clay Birds, Healings, and Sorcery Accusation
stories-5-110-jesus-cradle-speech-clay-b.note: In God's direct address to Jesus in 5:110, breathing life into a clay bird stands alongside speaking in the cradle and the Israelites calling his signs 'clear magic,' matching the Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2:2–4 and Talmud Sanhedrin 43a.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir read 5:110 as God's covenantal reminder to Jesus enumerating the miracles granted to him by divine permission (bi-idhni) to distinguish prophetic signs from divine sonship.
discussion.reply: Unlike 3:49, where Jesus announces these signs to Israel, 5:110 frames them as God's retrospective address and adds the Israelites' charge that his signs were 'clear magic.' That passage unites the second-century Infancy Gospel of Thomas 2:2–4 (animating clay sparrows) with the rabbinic verdict in Talmud Sanhedrin 43a that Jesus practiced sorcery and led Israel astray.

stories-5-110-jesus-cradle-speech-clay-b.quranEn: (Remember) when God said, ‘Jesus, son of Mary! Remember My blessing on you and on your mother, when I supported you with the holy spirit, (and) you spoke to the people (while you were still) in the cradle, and in adulthood. And when I taught you the Book and the wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel. And when you created the form of a bird from clay by My permission, and you breathed into it, and it became a bird by My permission, and you healed the blind and the leper by My permission. And when you brought forth the dead by My permission, and when I restrained the Sons of Israel from (violence against) you. When you brought them the clear signs, those among them who had disbelieved said, “This is nothing but clear magic.”’

sources.title: Infancy Gospel of Thomas
sources.en: And having made some soft clay, He fashioned out of it twelve sparrows. And it was the Sabbath when He did these things. And there were also many other children playing with Him. And a certain Jew, seeing what Jesus was doing, playing on the Sabbath , went off immediately, and said to his father Joseph: Behold, your son is at the stream, and has taken clay, and made of it twelve birds, and has profaned the Sabbath . And Joseph, coming to the place and seeing, cried out to Him, saying: Why do you do on the Sabbath what it is not lawful to do? And Jesus clapped His hands, and cried out to the sparrows, and said to them: Off you go! And the sparrows flew, and went off crying. And the Jews seeing this were amazed, and went away and reported to their chief men what they had seen Jesus doing.

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Sanhedrin
sources.en: Jesus the Nazarene is going out to be stoned because he practiced sorcery, incited people to idol worship, and led the Jewish people astray. Anyone who knows of a reason to acquit him should come forward and teach it on his behalf. And the court did not find a reason to acquit him, and so they stoned him and hung his corpse on Passover eve.

practices-5-3-carrion-blood-strangled-me.title: Dietary Code: Carrion, Blood, Pork, Strangled Meat, and Divination Arrows
practices-5-3-carrion-blood-strangled-me.note: Surah 5:3 expands the fourfold dietary ban with strangled, beaten, fallen, gored, and beast-torn animals alongside meat sacrificed on pagan stones and divination arrows, combining the Apostolic Decree of Acts 15:19–20 and the beast-torn flesh ban of Exodus 22:31.

discussion.view: Muslim scholars view Surah 5:3, revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage period, as the final completion of Islamic dietary law prohibiting both unslaughtered animals and pagan sacrificial and divinatory rites.
discussion.reply: Surah 5:3 brings together three distinct Near Eastern legal strata: the Apostolic Decree's ban on idol-offerings, blood, and strangled meat (Acts 15:19–20), the Torah prohibition on eating animals torn by wild beasts unless properly slaughtered (Exodus 22:31), and the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of partitioning camel meat with divination arrows (azlam) beside sacrificial stones (ansab).

practices-5-3-carrion-blood-strangled-me.quranEn: Forbidden to you (to eat) are: the dead (animal), and the blood, and swine’s flesh, and what has been dedicated to (a god) other than God, and the strangled (to death), and the beaten (to death), and the fallen (to death), and the gored (to death), and what a wild animal has devoured – except what you have slaughtered – and what has been sacrificed on stones. And (it is forbidden) that you should divide by divination arrows – that is wickedness for you. Today those who disbelieve have no hope of (ever destroying) your religion. So do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you, and I have completed My blessing on you, and I have approved Islam for you as a religion. But if anyone is forced by hunger, without intending to sin – surely God is forgiving, compassionate.
